assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model's electroweak sector and was a decades-long feat of detector design, trigger and calibration. The 2013 prize recognised the theory of the mechanism; the discovery itself has not been honoured, which makes this a natural, clear-cut experimental prize in my own area.
assessment.attribution: The discovery was made by two collaborations of thousands. The three credited founders of the ATLAS and CMS projects (Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee) conceived and led the detectors from the proposal stage. Gianotti, as ATLAS spokesperson at the time, is also a strong claim, so the choice of three of four names is contestable and I would leave it for discussion.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by two experiments and by a decade of Run 2 and Run 3 coupling measurements; the interpretation is stable and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether founders or the 2012 spokespeople best represent decisive credit
Prize rules cannot honour the collaborations, so any three-person selection will be seen as arbitrary by part of the community

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened a new observational window with the 2013 detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, followed by the 2017 TXS 0506+056 association and the 2022 Galactic-plane neutrino map. Building a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov detector in Antarctic ice was a remarkable instrumentation achievement and I regard this as a prime example of a new window on the Universe.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the project, Karle was central in the detector construction and the discovery analyses, and Spiering served as spokesperson and driver of the collaboration. The credited trio is a coherent set, though other collaborators and the earlier AMANDA and Baikal pioneers have claims.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed with multiple channels and the Galactic-plane result adds independent support. The individual source identifications are still few, so the field is still maturing, but the core discovery is robust.
uncertainties: Only a small number of sources are firmly identified
Credit relative to AMANDA and Baikal precursors and the wider collaboration

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, based on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, has improved timekeeping by orders of magnitude and reached fractional uncertainties around 1e-18. It enables tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a future redefinition of the second. It is a metrology result of clear, lasting importance and with direct use.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the early clocks; Ye brought the technique to record accuracy and many-body-interrogation regimes. This is a clean two-person attribution, although Hall and Hänsch were honoured in 2005 for the comb, which this builds on.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced and surpassed the performance, and the redefinition of the second is under way. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with ion-clock and comb contributions, such as Wineland's and Hänsch's, in how decisive the lattice idea is
Some of the strongest applications are still prospective

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration in electron lenses broke a limit that had held since Scherzer in 1936 and gave routine sub-ångström imaging of atoms in materials. This is a textbook case of an instrument advance that changed what can be measured, and it is widely used in condensed-matter and materials physics.
assessment.attribution: Rose provided the theoretical design of the correctors, Haider and Urban built and demonstrated them, and the three were jointly honoured by the Wolf Prize and the Kavli Prize. This gives a natural, well-supported three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Commercial instruments are everywhere, so confirmation and impact are fully established. Some may see it as closer to chemistry or materials science, but the physics is electron optics.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the subject as physics rather than instrumentation for materials and chemistry
Contributions from Krivanek and others to different corrector geometries

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors underpin vertex and tracking systems at essentially every modern collider experiment, including the Higgs discovery and flavour physics, and have spread to medical and X-ray imaging. As a detector builder I consider this one of the most consequential and least recognised enabling technologies in particle physics.
assessment.attribution: Parker pioneered microstrip detectors, Heijne and Jarron led the hybrid pixel work at CERN. The credit is plausible but others, such as Kemmer for planar processing and the Medipix and ALICE pixel teams, also contributed, so allocation is not tidy.
assessment.maturity: The technology has been proven for decades. Timing is fine, although the Committee has rarely honoured detector technology on its own, and I would have to persuade colleagues.
uncertainties: Multiple strong claimants, for example Kemmer and the pixel groups
Prize precedent for pure detector technology is limited, as with Charpak in 1992

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* directly show the shadow of a black hole and test strong-field gravity. It is a heroic exercise in global VLBI instrumentation, calibration and imaging, with obvious public impact.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the EHT instrument and collaboration, and Falcke championed the shadow concept and the science case. Narayan's theoretical modelling is also important, but I limit myself to two names for the observational core. Credit within a 200-plus member collaboration remains hard to divide.
assessment.maturity: Results are recent, with the first image in 2019 and Sgr A* in 2022. Polarisation and multi-epoch data are building confirmation, but the independent verification is limited because only one collaboration can do this. Probably a little early.
uncertainties: Only one collaboration, hence limited independent replication
Fair attribution among theory, instrument and imaging teams

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered the first precision full-sky CMB maps and fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model at the percent level, and its measurements of the age, composition and geometry of the Universe were transformative. It is a flagship space instrument result.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission as PI, Page was a key instrument scientist and Spergel led cosmological interpretation. The configuration is sensible. The 2006 prize to Mather and Smoot and the 2019 prize to Peebles cover neighbouring ground, so the committee may feel the area has been recognised.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and superseded by Planck, so the result is very mature. Because of that, the case rests on historical priority.
uncertainties: Overlap with prizes already awarded in CMB cosmology
Other leaders, such as Wilkinson and the WMAP team, are not among the credited names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2023 pulsar timing array evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens the gravitational spectrum beyond LIGO's band, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries, using the Galaxy as a detector. It is a beautiful measurement built on years of patient timing and systematics control.
assessment.attribution: The result comes from several collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA), and none of the three credited people alone can represent them. Kramer leads the European effort, McLaughlin and Siemens NANOGrav. Credit allocation among the teams would be hard.
assessment.maturity: Evidence is at roughly 3 to 4 sigma, the Hellings-Downs correlation is not yet at discovery significance, and the source of the signal is uncertain. I consider recognition premature, so this sits at the bottom of my list.
uncertainties: Significance is below the discovery threshold and the astrophysical origin is unsettled
Credit is split across several collaborations
